Everyone remembers the storm... but I remember seeing something bright red snapping wildly in the gale winds near the shore bamboo pole. It was a warning flag.

I remember an older fisherman running toward the coast right when the red warning flag was raised. He didn't go out to fish—he went to secure the other men's boats so they wouldn't smash! Look nearby for that red flag.

When I was little, I saw the coastguard tie a red cloth flag to warn us of typhoon winds. A brave father saw it and rushed down to save a stranded boy's banca. A fragment of that warning flag lies right over there.
That afternoon, the wind roared so loud you couldn't hear the church bells. The red weather flag was tearing apart on its pole. Check the ground nearby—the memory of that red flag is shining.
My mother always said someone tried to signal the outer boats before the waves grew monstrous. He raised the weather flag himself when no one else dared step into the storm. Search close by!
